framework.name: Strategic Priority 1 - GOVERNANCE, HUMAN RIGHT, PEACE & SECURITY
framework.description:
Strategic Intent: All Nigerians enjoy good and inclusive governance and human rights in secure, resilient and peaceful communities.
The  UN system in Nigeria will place premium and special focus on increasing citizens confidence and engagement in governance and public service delivery mechanisms, by supporting the fight against corruption and reinforcing the accountability framework.

The UN system will leverage on its networks and partnerships with stakeholders to provide quality advisory service, youth and women participation in peace processes, capacity strengthening, and technical support for conflict prevention, mediation and reconciliation, psychosocial support through the establishment of early warning mechanisms/responses and the national peace architecture.

children.name: Outcome 1.1 - Good Governance and Rule of Law
children.description: Good governance and the rule of law are essential preconditions for the fulfillment of peace and stability, without which societies cannot function, let alone flourish. The commitment to transparency and accountability mitigates corruption and reinforces rule of law. Hence creating economic opportunities which in turn stimulates growth.

framework.name: Strategic Priority 2 - Equitable Quality Basic Services
framework.description:
Strategic Intent: Nigerians enjoy improved well-being through sustainable, equitable and quality basic social and protection services which fulfill their human rights and contribute to greater social cohesion and economic development.

The UN system in Nigeria envisions that all Nigerians will realize their human rights and access quality basic services in an equitable manner. Availability and accessibility of sustainable, equitable and quality basic social protection services will contribute to greater social cohesion and economic development. Since the result area covers several sectors, the specific strategies chosen in a particular year will depend on the needs, geographic focus and a balance between upstream policy work and downstream implementation.

children.name: Outcome 2.1 - Health, Nutrition, and HIV/AIDS
children.description: While health, including nutrition and access to HIV services, is a basic human right, the majority of Nigerians have limited access to realize this entitlement. Through the UNSDCF UN will contribute towards addressing the challenges in health, nutrition, and HIV/AIDS sectors. So it is expected that by 2022, Nigerians , with focus on most disadvantaged, have access and use quality health, nutrition and HIV & AIDS services.

framework.name: Strategic Priority 3 - Sustainable Inclusive Economic Growth & Development
framework.description:
Strategic intent: Nigerians have improved living standard characterized by inclusive and diversified economic growth, effective population management, food security and environmental sustainability.

The UN System will assist Nigeria to address the identified challenges in this result area, through joint action and based on its comparative advantage by mobilizing support to develop appropriate policies, plans and regulatory frameworks aimed at sustainable and inclusive economic growth and development in the country. The UN will support the Government in this result area by providing strategic interventions for the diversification of the economy, effective management and utilization of human resources, food security and environmental sustainability.

projects.name: 1.2.4.6 - Support the UN Joint Basket Fund for Covid-19 pandemic response
projects.description: UNDP: The One UN Response to COVID-19 in Nigeria Project seeks to support national efforts towards optimum care of confirmed COVID-19 cases and to contain the spread of the outbreak through an inclusive and nationally owned response based on best practices from previous health emergencies as well as lessons learned and experiences from other countries during the COVID-19 crisis. Using the One UN approach, the project’s objective will be realized through six outputs: Output 1: Improved rapid procurement of disease commodity packages for surveillance, prevention and control, and clinical management; Output 2: Complementary ongoing risk communication strategies for sustained community engagement and cooperation (RCCE) are supported; Output 3: Development of tailored and decentralized response strategies at the state level that are aligned with the coordinated framework at the federal level supported; Output 4: Access to essential health services maintained through socio-economic analytics and proactive early recovery and social protection activities targeting vulnerable groups; Output 5: Capacities for R&D and modelling strengthened; Output 6: Coordination of partnerships and mobilization of resources for collective response improved. The project is enabled by support from public and private sector resources channelled through the One UN COVID-19 Response Basket Fund with WHO, UNICEF, UNDP, UN Women, UNFPA, UNAIDS, UNIDO and ILO as the participating UN agencies (PUNOs).

In partnership with and guided by the Nigerian authorities and stakeholders, UNODC has been implementing a multi-phased programme of technical assistance since 2012. projects.description:
RECONCILIATION AND REINTEGRATION OF FORMER ARMED NON-STATE COMBATANTS AND BOKO HARAM ASSOCIATES (S2R)	// Project Number: 00120397 // 1 January -  30 November 2022												
This project aims to enhance community preparedness for reintegration and reduction of rejection and stigmatisation of former associates in selected areas in Adamawa, Borno and Yobe States, preparing ground for community-based healing and reconciliation. The main outputs that the project seeks to achieve include: Communities are sensitised and prepared for reconciliation and reintegration; Community-level transitional / restorative justice mechanisms are developed; Conflict-sensitive community-prioritised livelihoods are created for the most vulnerable, low risk associates and non-state security providers; Stratified community-led activities increase community cohesiveness and coping mechanisms for the most vulnerable, low risk associates and non-state security providers; Process developed for non-state security providers to be disarmed, demobilised and reintegrated; Inclusive, responsive and accountable structures to manage DDRR activities are created between and across the various levels of government and communities. Specific interventions that will contribute to these outputs include: widespread advocacy and awareness campaigns; design and deployment of reconciliation and reintegration platforms, committees and volunteer groups; community-based and led reconciliation and restorative justice processes; strengthening community-level “peace dividends” advancing interventions in the form of community-led social impact project that help to build resilience to violence; and a multiple targeting approach, where selected community members received targeted assistance (along with low-risk former NSAG associates and CTJF/vigilante group members)."

RECONCILIATION AND REINTEGRATION OF FORMER ARMED NON-STATE COMBATANTS AND BOKO HARAM ASSOCIATES (S2R)	// Project Number: 00120397 // 1 January -  30 November 2022

projects.name: 1.1.2.10 - Strengthening Nigeria’s response to the trafficking of wildlife and forestry products.
projects.description:
In recent years, Nigeria has evolved into a primary transit hub for trafficking in illicit wildlife products. According to the UNODC World Wildlife Crime Report 2020, Nigeria has emerged as one of the leading source and transit point for the illicit trafficking in elephant tusks, pangolin scales, rosewood (Pterocarpus Erinaceus, known in Nigeria as “kosso”) and other endangered wildlife and forest products. 

To support the Government of Nigeria in tackling wildlife and forest crime, UNODC, with the support of the Government of Germany, is partnering with the Federal Ministry of Environment, the Nigeria Customs Service, the National Environmental Standards and Regulations Enforcement Agency (NESREA) and  other state and non-state actors to implement the Project, “Strengthening Nigeria’s Response to the Trafficking of Wildlife and Forestry Products”. The project commenced implementation in July 2020 and is expected to run for 30 months till 31 December 2022. The Project has three main outcome areas: Outcome 1: National policy frameworks and domestic coordination to address wildlife and forest crime strengthened; Outcome 2: Capacity of frontline officers to detect and intercept illegal shipments of wildlife improved; and Outcome 3: Prosecutorial and judicial capacity to investigate, prosecute and adjudicate wildlife and forest crime strengthened.

projects.name: 2.1.2.29 - Support to HIV and health services in prisons and among people who use drugs
projects.description:
Globally, HIV prevalence and new infections have drastically reduced however, Nigeria ranks third among the countries with high number of people living with HIV with an estimated 1.8 million people living with the infection in 2019. While some of the drivers of new infections in the society include low condom use, gender inequality and multiple sexual partners, new infections among people who use drugs and people in custodial centres are attributed to sharing of needles and other paraphernalia, drug use in custodial centres, forced sex and unprotected sexual intercourse in custodial centres amongst others.

People who inject drugs (PWIDs) are also particularly vulnerable to HIV and AIDS. According to UNODC survey on drug use in Nigeria, 9% of PWIDs in Nigeria live with HIV and AIDS. Prevention of the negative health and social consequences of drug use is critical for both drug users and the society at large. The introduction and scaling up of core interventions as outlined in the WHO, UNODC, UNAIDS “Technical Guide for Countries to Set Targets for Universal Access to HIV Prevention, Treatment and Care for Injecting Drug Users”, are important measures for prevention, treatment, and care of HIV among PWIDs in the community and in prison settings.

To effectively address the above, UNODC Country Office in Nigeria is supporting the Government of Nigeria on HIV testing services in Nigeria custodial centres, HIV care in prisons and linkages to healthcare in the community, Harm reduction and drug demand reduction activities (i.e Needle and Syringe Programme, Opioids Substitution Therapy) and in the conduct of further studies relating to HIV and drug use.

projects.description:
UNESCO facilitated the participation of Nigeria in the e-Learning training on “ Flood Early Waring, Flood Hazard Mapping and Contingency Planning”. This training will enable Nigeria, set up and operate flood early warning systems. Participation included Nigerian Emergency management Agency (NEMA), National Water Resources Institute (NWRI), Nigerian Hydrological service Agency (NIHSA) and Regional Center for Integrated River Basin management (RC-IRBM)  
In 2020 a high level online Advocacy event tagged “Water and Climate Change: Women’s Coping Strategies In West Africa, was organized via zoom platform. This Online event was jointly organized by UNESCO Multisectoral Regional Office Abuja, UNESCO World Water Assessment Programme (WWAP) Perugia-Italy and UNESCO Category II Center namely; Regional Center for Integrated River Basin Management IRC-IRBM), Kaduna-Nigeria.   Participants/target beneficiaries included water and gender 35 experts from Nigeria ( Men 20: Women 15), The  event featured presentation of the 2019 WWAP Toolkit on sex-disaggregated water data.  “The toolkit contains a priority topic on water, migration, displacement and climate change, dedicated indicators and the related questions for the collection of data in the field, making it a valuable tool for the collection of much-needed and currently scarce sex-disaggregated water data. The tool kit will be used for the two technical trainings in 2021.

projects.name: 1.2.3.2 - Support for reconciliation and reintegration of former Armed Non-State combatants and Boko Haram associates.
projects.description:
RECONCILIATION AND REINTEGRATION OF FORMER ARMED NON-STATE COMBATANTS AND BOKO HARAM ASSOCIATES (S2R)	// Project Number: 00120397 // 1 January -  30 November 2022												
This project aims to enhance community preparedness for reintegration and reduction of rejection and stigmatisation of former associates in selected areas in Adamawa, Borno and Yobe States, preparing ground for community-based healing and reconciliation. The main outputs that the project seeks to achieve include: Communities are sensitised and prepared for reconciliation and reintegration; Community-level transitional / restorative justice mechanisms are developed; Conflict-sensitive community-prioritised livelihoods are created for the most vulnerable, low risk associates and non-state security providers; Stratified community-led activities increase community cohesiveness and coping mechanisms for the most vulnerable, low risk associates and non-state security providers; Process developed for non-state security providers to be disarmed, demobilised and reintegrated; Inclusive, responsive and accountable structures to manage DDRR activities are created between and across the various levels of government and communities. Specific interventions that will contribute to these outputs include: widespread advocacy and awareness campaigns; design and deployment of reconciliation and reintegration platforms, committees and volunteer groups; community-based and led reconciliation and restorative justice processes; strengthening community-level “peace dividends” advancing interventions in the form of community-led social impact project that help to build resilience to violence; and a multiple targeting approach, where selected community members received targeted assistance (along with low-risk former NSAG associates and CTJF/vigilante group members)."
projects.outcome: Output 1.2.3 - Citizen Engagement platforms and dialogue with national and non-state actors at all levels increased to achieve peaceful coexistence
